source.title: Random Label Prediction Heads for Studying Memorization in Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Marlon Becker; Jonas Konrad; Luis Garcia Rodriguez; Benjamin Risse

record.tranche_reason: The study compares full-network random-label training with its auxiliary random-label prediction head, using a different measurement setup to examine random-label fitting.
record.gate_note: The study reports results from training a full network on random labels in Figure A.17, but the figure supplies no textual numeric result. The RLP-head and regularizer results measure auxiliary-head predictions during training on class labels; they do not establish direct full-network fitting of randomly labeled data. The paper also discusses cited results from prior work, which are not extracted as this study's results.
record.test_reason: Appendix A.15 trains WideResNet-16-w networks end-to-end on completely random labels using SGD and measures training accuracy, directly testing V1 with the original type of method and measure. The supplied figure text does not reveal the achieved accuracies, so it cannot establish near-perfect fitting.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors propose auxiliary random-label accuracy as a memorization and complexity metric, validate it against full-network random-label training, and find that reducing this metric can improve or impair generalization depending on the setting. They also report that final-layer regularization can shift memorization and class-level abstraction into earlier layers.
record.recipe_differences: The main method trains an auxiliary random-label prediction head alongside a classifier trained on true labels. Appendix A.15 also compares that measure with end-to-end full-network training on random labels; the text reports correlation but gives no numeric result in the supplied figure description.
record.method_sensitivity: The study says the capacity of the RLP-head and the number of random labels affect measured random-label accuracy; it also reports different effects of RLP-regularization across datasets and settings.

fits_no_version.finding: During true-label training, the auxiliary RLP-head reaches approximately 70% random-label accuracy for ViT-B/32 on ImageNet; its accuracy depends on head capacity, label count, network width, and attachment depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random labels can be decoded from representations learned during true-label training, with decoding performance dependent on the probe and representation.

fits_no_version.finding: RLP-regularization can improve or impair test performance depending on dataset and training conditions; regularizing the final layer can shift auxiliary-head memorization signals into earlier layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suppressing auxiliary random-label predictability has setting-dependent effects on generalization and on where sample-specific information is decodable.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix A.14 reports that weight decay drives both auxiliary random-label accuracy and training accuracy on the 10% noisy-label subset close to zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explicit regularization can suppress noisy-label memorization in partially corrupted ImageNet training; this does not establish prevention of fitting a completely random labeling.

record.problems: The direct full-network random-label comparison is shown only in a figure and described qualitatively; the text provides no numeric training or test error for that experiment. Most random-label results use an auxiliary head while the main network trains on true labels, so they do not directly establish the full-network random-label fitting conditions in V1.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained. Figure A.17 is a qualitative correlation comparison without textual numeric results or a stated training/test error outcome for full-network random-label training. Other reported RLP-head measurements use an auxiliary head during true-label training and do not test the versions as worded.

untested.parts: Chance test error and an explicit verification that architecture and training hyperparameters remain unchanged between true-label and random-label training. Full-network training accuracy is measured, but its values cannot be read from the supplied text.
Relative training time for true versus random labels and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Training-set fitting of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit throughout a corruption sweep extending to fully random labels, together with steadily increasing test error toward chance.
Whether weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation prevent fitting a completely randomly labeled training set, and whether removing them alone makes true-label generalization poor.
A direct comparison establishing that shared real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels are memorized. Auxiliary-head learning curves probe a different training setup.

record.verdict_notes: Figure A.17 explicitly reports Pearson's r = 0.93, correcting the record's suggestion that the comparison has no numerical result. This correlation does not establish zero or near-zero random-label training error. Its full-network accuracy results are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not duplicated under missing. No verdict is justified from unreadable plotted accuracies or from auxiliary-head results substituted for full-network random-label fitting.

versions.untested_parts: Whether full networks reach zero or near-zero training error, have chance test error, retain the original architecture and training hyperparameters, and generalize well on true labels.
Training-time comparison with true labels and convergence as the fraction of corrupted labels changes.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
A sweep from no label corruption to fully random labels with perfect training fit and steadily increasing test error.
Whether those regularizers prevent standard networks from fitting randomly labeled data, and whether removing them by itself harms true-label generalization.
Whether models learn real-label patterns before memorizing random or noisy labels, with a direct comparison of those learning dynamics.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
